synthesis.body: Starlight renders the full guide sidebar on every page, so a document-wide href scan over an emitted page proves nothing about a particular section. A case asserting that the relocated catalogue-extension section still linked to its four guides passed under a mutation that deleted one of those step links, because the sidebar carried the same href; it only failed once scoped to the section's own nodes. Two mechanics make the scoping work. First, heading ids resolve through a wrapper: Starlight emits <div class="sl-heading-wrapper level-hN"> around each heading, and section content are siblings of that WRAPPER, not of the heading -- walking the heading's own siblings yields only the anchor icon and an empty section. Second, the slug is not the obvious one: '### P2 - Shape what to build - ~3 hours' emits id="p2--shape-what-to-build--3-hours", because github-slugger drops the punctuation and keeps the spaces that surrounded it, so a slugifier that collapses whitespace runs to a single hyphen derives a different anchor than the site serves.

title: A document-wide href scan cannot prove a link sits in a section: the Starlight sidebar carries every href
